kfics_assessment.pdf.what: KFICS Facilities Assessment for Bourbon County Schools, prepared by RossTarrant Architects, presented at the July 2026 facility planning meeting (38 slides). Per-school needs (building condition plus instructional deficiency): BCHS $27,488,455; BCMS $22,418,692; Cane Ridge $14,387,595; Bourbon Central $8,840,267; North Middletown $8,530,093 ($5,648,434 condition + $2,881,659 instructional); Preschool $7,861,696; Agriculture Building $1,825,444. District total $98,441,294 ($91,352,242 school centers + $7,089,052 support). Slide capacities: BCHS 704, BCMS 544, Bourbon Central 499, Cane Ridge 397, North Middletown 154, Preschool 160 (note: the 2026 draft DFP table prints 640 and 547 for the two Paris elementaries, a discrepancy between the district's own documents).
kfics_assessment.pdf.source: presentation file shared from the district facility planning process

bond_2024_sfcc_disclosure.pdf.what: SFCC Bond Payee Disclosure for the Bourbon County School District Finance Corporation School Building Revenue Bonds, Series of 2024, submitted to the School Facilities Construction Commission and reviewed by the legislature's Capital Projects and Bond Oversight Committee on June 20, 2024. States the purpose: various construction projects including roof replacement at Bourbon County High School and a districtwide audio system. Presented at $10,000,000 estimated (18 percent SFCC share, $132,646 estimated annual state debt service; $633,142 local); sold at $6,055,000. No tax increase required. Expected Moody's A1; bond counsel Steptoe & Johnson; fiscal agent Baird; competitive sale projected August 2024.
bond_2024_sfcc_disclosure.pdf.source: Kentucky Legislative Research Commission, Capital Projects and Bond Oversight Committee documents, June 2024 meeting (apps.legislature.ky.gov/CommitteeDocuments/13), item 6.D; pages excerpted from the SFCC transmittal.

cpboc_minutes_2024_06_20.pdf.what: Minutes of the Kentucky Capital Projects and Bond Oversight Committee, June 20, 2024, recording approval of six SFCC school-district debt issues including Bourbon County by roll-call vote.

munis_cost_by_org_fy2026.pdf.what: The district's own MUNIS general ledger, Cost by ORG transaction detail, fiscal 2026 (203 pages): every expenditure transaction with its full fund-org-function-object account string, vendor, dates and signed amount, plus the first-page org summary (six school orgs totalling $21,482,444.56; org 090 NMES $1,285,310.36). Source of the FY2026 actuals used in the school's General Fund table, the reconciliation bridge, the breakeven bars, and the closure grid's fixed-position lever. Parsed reproducibly by build/munis_extract.py, which validates its own parse against the report's summary to the penny; extract archived as build/munis_nmes_fy2026.json.
munis_cost_by_org_fy2026.pdf.source: District records production (Cost by ORG report, produced July 2026).

baird_lpc_june2026.pdf.what: Bonding Capacity Presentation by Robert W. Baird & Co., the district's financial advisor, to the Local Planning Committee, June 2026 (8 pages). Rates current bonding capacity at $32 million from $3,252,893 of FY2027 bondable restricted revenues (FSPK nickel $1,200,105 + recallable nickel $1,200,105 + state equalization $552,990 + 80 percent capital outlay $173,944 + $126,250 of unexpired SFCC offers, expiring January 2028 through January 2034). Sensitivities: a loss of 50 students drops capacity to $31 million (about $20,000 of capacity per student); rates 100bp lower raise it to $35 million. Outstanding debt $14,420,000 total ($13,066,437 district share), including the 2024 bond with a General-Fund-paid debt service column of about $231,000 a year. Assumes the 2026-27 Forecast SEEK Report (AADA 2,174.3), $679 FSPK equalization, HB 757 sunset FY2046, conservative June 15 2026 rates.
baird_lpc_june2026.pdf.source: District facility planning process, LPC meeting materials, June 2026.

records_fulfilled_2026_07.pdf.what: The district's index of records fulfilled in response to the July 2026 open records requests (5 pages, received July 20-21, 2026). Key answers: N/A for any cost-benefit analysis of closing, consolidating, or repurposing the school; N/A for enrollment studies, capacity studies, feasibility studies, financial analyses, cost comparisons, transportation studies, ride-time analyses, GIS boundary files, and any document evaluating the future use of NMES. Produced: the MUNIS Cost by ORG ledger, working budgets FY2024-FY2026, salary schedules 2023-2026, payroll expenditure reports, current bus routes (NMES AM and PM streets), enrollment summaries and projections, the KFICS assessment, DFP drafts, LPC records, and the superintendent's contract.
records_fulfilled_2026_07.pdf.source: District records custodian, response to the open records requests of July 2026.
